newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Jan 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Jan 23.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- U.S. Central Bank chairman Alan Greenspan's remarks appearing to play down the threat of inflation reverberated around world markets on Wednesday, depressing the gold price and making the rand and capital markets firm sharply.
- Government and public service unions are set to clash during negotiations next week over a plan to end a moratorium on forced lay-offs in the public service.
- The rand could prove "very stable" this year, declining by less than inflation differentials, Reserve Bank governor Chris Stals said.
- The Registrar of Banks is to monitor the financial position of foreign banks' representative offices from March this year, in a move to ensure they do not break rules in competing with local banks.

- No decision would be taken on the controversial three billion rand Syrian arms deal until Deputy President Thabo Mbeki had considered a host of issues, including the technology involved and U.S. legislation, cabinet secretary Jakes Gerwel said.
BUSINESS REPORT

- The rand's strength continued unchecked on Wednesday as the currency improved more than two cents against the dollar to reach a seven and a half week high of 4.6325 rand in late trade, from 4.6545 on Tuesday.

- Tyre importers would fiercely oppose a call for a 66 percent duty to be levied on imported tyres -- a proposal by South Africa's four major tyre manufacturers -- a spokesman for a group of 14 importers said.

- The Development Bank of Southern Africa and the department of finance have agreed in principle to refinance the 3.1 bllion rand debt of former apartheid homelands on the bank's books at higher interest rates to strengthen the bank's capital base, Stan Davis, the finance department's director, said.
- Three senior employees of the Standard Corporate and Merchant Bank (SCMB) coprporate finance team have left the bank to join financial services group Capital Alliance (Captall), SCMB announced.

- The continued weakness in the gold price during the coming weeks might result in Anglo American having to renegotiate terms of the sale of 34.9 percent of JCI Ltd to African Mining Group, analysts said.
THE STAR
- The University of Pretoria said a new AIDS treatment announced by a team of researchers had yet to be properly tested.
- Local doctors expressed disbelief at the AIDS-drug breakthrough and criticised the way the findings were released.
SAKE-BEELD
- Large industrial groups have approached electricity supplier Eskom for permission to pay their bills directly, rather than through their local councils.

- The managing director of Automakers Ltd, Marinus Daling, said the company had made several mistakes since listing on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, chief among them underestimating the competition in the autmobile industry.
- Former finance minister Chris Liebenberg has been appointed chairman of Nedcor banking group.
- Khula business financing company has reached guarantee agreements with local banks in an effort to help small firms with financing.

- Reserve Bank governor Chris Stals said he saw scope for a "very stable" rand in 1997, with a fall this year less than the inflation differentials between South Africa and its major trading partners.
